result.note: Tests the location of GRSE's new Raichak yard and details of the August 2026 defence shipbuilding expansion projects.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh broke ground on a new Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) yard able to build warships up to 200 metres long. Where is this yard located?
questions.explain: GRSE's new 32-acre yard is at Raichak in West Bengal. It will let GRSE bid for next-generation destroyers alongside commercial vessels. Ishapore is where Yantra India Limited is adding forging presses.
questions.source: GRSE's new 32-acre yard at Raichak in West Bengal will build warships up to 200 metres long, letting it bid for next-generation destroyers alongside commercial vessels.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the defence-industrial expansion projects launched in West Bengal in August 2026:
items: The five projects, worth about INR 35 billion, are at Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers and Yantra India Limited.
Yantra India Limited's new forging presses at Ishapore will produce gun barrels and naval-weapon components.
Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers has built over 800 vessels to date, most of them for the Indian Coast Guard.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: most of GRSE's more than 800 vessels were built for the Indian Navy, not the Coast Guard. Rajnath Singh called ship repair and overhaul the low-hanging fruit and urged India to become a maintenance hub for the Indian Ocean region.
questions.source: GRSE has built over 800 vessels to date, most for the Indian Navy.
